PullRequest.Title: Chat input pills: only rescan the row when its state changes
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #347904

## Problem

`ChatInputPills` derives the pills row state (`visible`, `empty` or `hidden`) and applies it with `recomputeInitiallyAndOnChange`. That calls its handler on every update of the pill sources, even when the derived state is unchanged. While a response streams, the sources update with almost every chunk. Each handler call runs `DomScrollableElement.scanDomNode`, which reads `clientWidth`/`scrollWidth` and often forces a synchronous layout.

I measured this with a layout probe on Insiders 1.147.0 in the Agents window, using a mock LLM endpoint. Over one streamed response there were 320 rescans, 52 ms in total, and 43 of them forced a layout.

## Change

The state handler now runs in an `autorun` that reads the derived row state. The DOM work only happens when the state actually changes. Pill size changes are still rescanned by the row's existing resize observer, so overflow and scroll arrows keep updating when pills grow, shrink or are added. Focus restore on hide is unchanged.

## Tests

A regression test checks that updating pill data without changing the row state no longer rescans the row.

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatInputPills.test.ts`
  - With the fix: 32 passing.
  - Without the fix (production file reverted to `main`): 31 passing, 1 failing ("does not rescan the row when pill data updates without changing the row state").
- The layout probe on a dev build of this branch no longer shows `scanDomNode` from the pills row while a response streams. Before: 293 calls on a dev build of `main`, 320 on Insiders.

The UI after-evidence is a probe and unit-test result, not a recorded run.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Every live pill-source update invoked synchronous scrollbar geometry reads even when row visibility/emptiness was unchanged, multiplying layout work by streaming update count.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Streaming an agent response caused hundreds of unnecessary row rescans and dozens of forced layouts, adding measurable main-thread layout time.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added autorun reads a separately derived scalar rowState. Derived uses strict equality and only notifies the autorun when that state changes, so source updates that merely alter pill data no longer execute DOM class updates or scanDomNode. Actual pill size changes remain covered by ChatPillsRow's ResizeObserver, while visibility-state transitions still scan once.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 534 called ChatPillsRow.scanDomNode from a derived(...).recomputeInitiallyAndOnChange callback. Observable KeepAliveObserver invokes that callback at the end of every dependency update, regardless of whether the derived 'visible'/'empty'/'hidden' value changed. AgentHostSessionInputPills feeds ChatInputPills from live session/chat subscriptions and derived artifact/reference/change sources, so streaming state updates repeatedly reached this callback. ChatPillsRow.scanDomNode delegates to DomScrollableElement.scanDomNode, which synchronously reads clientWidth, scrollWidth, clientHeight, and scrollHeight. The PR's layout probe reports 320 rescans, 43 forced layouts, and 52 ms over one streamed response, matching the traced mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent response streaming updates session-status pill data while the row remains visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An already-established Agent Host chat-state subscription publishes an update; observable pill sources and ChatPillsWidget update, then rowState is recomputed. Before the PR, the row handler synchronously scanned scrollbar geometry on every update. After the PR, source-only updates stop at rowState equality and the DOM scan is off this update path unless the scalar row state changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Maintain the existing StateComponents.Chat subscription and receive live chat-state updates from the Agent Host connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One persistent subscription for the active chat; many notifications can arrive during one streamed response, but the diff neither creates nor duplicates the subscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single subscription supplied updates, and every relevant update could trigger a synchronous row scan even when visibility/emptiness was unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The inbound notification precedes pill recomputation, but this PR adds no request/round trip. It removes synchronous layout work after notifications whose derived row state is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost previously scaled with live subscription notification/chunk count, independent of effective pill-row state changes. After the change it scales with the much smaller number of transitions among visible, empty, and hidden; size changes are handled by the existing ResizeObserver.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Inbound subscription updates and observable reactions are serialized on the UI thread. There is one ChatInputPills row for the active Agent Host chat; no fan-out or new parallel work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is added or bypassed. The derived rowState remains observed and uses strict scalar equality; both cold initialization and the first real state transition run the handler, while warm same-state updates are coalesced by derived equality.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: observable internals prove recomputeInitiallyAndOnChange invokes its callback on every dependency update, derived strict equality suppresses unchanged rowState notifications, and scanDomNode reads client/scroll dimensions synchronously.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact notification counts and forced-layout duration vary by response and browser layout state, but the synchronous geometry-read mechanism and per-notification pre-diff multiplicity are directly established; the supplied probe reports hundreds of scans for one response.
Scenarios.Verdict: This is a verified performance fix, not a regression. No finding is warranted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pills appear, disappear, or all become filtered/hidden, changing the row between visible, empty, and hidden
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The pill/visibility observable changes rowState; the autorun immediately updates classes, focusability, persistent-row visibility, and performs one scan before the UI state transition completes. This preserves the pre-diff critical-path work only for actual row-state transitions.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the number of row-state transitions, not the number of source or entry updates. The scalar state has only three values and no collection-size-dependent boundary calls are introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous autorun on the UI thread per committed state transition; observable transactions coalesce dependency propagation and there is no concurrent fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: rowState's cached strict-equality value suppresses duplicate state notifications. There are no positive/negative data caches or external cache misses on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed autorun directly reads only rowState, and the unchanged scan remains inside that transition handler.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of user-driven hide/filter transitions varies, but each transition intentionally retains one geometry scan and constant DOM state updates.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: required synchronous work remains bounded to actual state changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Visible pill labels, entries, or dimensions change without changing row visibility
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatPillsWidget updates rendered pill DOM; ChatPillsRow's existing ResizeObserver observes the pills element/content and runs layout/scan when dimensions actually change. The new rowState autorun is skipped, so redundant synchronous scanning is removed from the source-update stack and dimension handling remains observer-driven.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Widget rendering can scale with pill count as before. Row scans now scale with actual resize deliveries rather than every data update; no new per-pill IPC, filesystem, network, or subprocess work is present.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM rendering and observer callbacks are serialized by the browser/UI thread. Resize notifications can batch multiple DOM changes; there is no added timer, queue, or unbounded concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No external cache participates. Automatic-compaction measurements are invalidated only by existing resize/mutation handling; the diff does not alter that lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ChatInputPills calls ChatPillsRow.observe on the pills element, and ChatPillsRow's ResizeObserver invalidates measurements and calls layout, which scans the DOM.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser ResizeObserver batching and exact layout cost vary, but source inspection establishes that the observed pills element is already registered and its callback calls layout/scan.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the existing resize path covers dimension changes while the diff removes duplicate eager scans.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced observable propagation, row resize/layout ownership, the Agent Host subscription caller, and synchronous geometry reads. No diff-introduced performance issue was found. Recorded the PR as a high-confidence fix for repeated synchronous layout scans during streamed updates.
